01-hartford-newsboys.jpg.title: Hartford Newsboys
01-hartford-newsboys.jpg.alt: Hartford Newsboys: an open-access photograph from the National Gallery of Art.
01-hartford-newsboys.jpg.description: Lewis Hine. Hartford Newsboys, 1909. National Gallery of Art.

02-addie-card-12-years-old-spinner-in-co.title: Addie Card, 12 years old. Spinner in cotton mill, North Pownal, Vermont
02-addie-card-12-years-old-spinner-in-co.alt: This sepia-toned photograph depicts a young girl standing next to a piece of machinery in an industrial setting.
02-addie-card-12-years-old-spinner-in-co.description: Lewis Hine. Addie Card, 12 years old. Spinner in cotton mill, North Pownal, Vermont, 1910. National Gallery of Art.

03-at-the-close-of-the-day-pennsylvania..title: At the Close of the Day, Pennsylvania
03-at-the-close-of-the-day-pennsylvania..alt: The image shows a group of miners outside the entrance of a mine.
03-at-the-close-of-the-day-pennsylvania..description: Lewis Hine. At the Close of the Day, Pennsylvania, January 7, 1911. National Gallery of Art.

04-8-30-p-m-group-of-newsboys-selling-at.title: 8:30 P.M. Group of newsboys selling at the depot, Hartford, Connecticut. Smallest boy 11 years old.
04-8-30-p-m-group-of-newsboys-selling-at.alt: The image depicts six young boys standing in front of a building.
04-8-30-p-m-group-of-newsboys-selling-at.description: Lewis Hine. 8:30 P.M. Group of newsboys selling at the depot, Hartford, Connecticut. Smallest boy 11 years old., March 1909. National Gallery of Art.

05-john-pento-14-years-old-daniel-and-an.title: John Pento, 14 years old, Daniel and Angelo Pento, 7 years old, selling newspapers, Hartford, Connecticut
05-john-pento-14-years-old-daniel-and-an.alt: Three boys are standing against a textured wall, with their full bodies visible.
05-john-pento-14-years-old-daniel-and-an.description: Lewis Hine. John Pento, 14 years old, Daniel and Angelo Pento, 7 years old, selling newspapers, Hartford, Connecticut, March 1909. National Gallery of Art.

06-title-from-caption-on-object-read-all.title: Title from caption on object: "Read All About It!"
06-title-from-caption-on-object-read-all.alt: Title from caption on object: "Read All About It!": an open-access photograph from the National Gallery of Art.
06-title-from-caption-on-object-read-all.description: Lewis Hine. Title from caption on object: "Read All About It!", April 1912. National Gallery of Art.

01-soldier-thrown-in-air.jpg.title: Soldier Thrown in Air
01-soldier-thrown-in-air.jpg.alt: This black-and-white photograph shows a group of men in dark shirts with dark, wide-brimmed hats.
01-soldier-thrown-in-air.jpg.description: Lewis Hine. Soldier Thrown in Air, 1917. National Gallery of Art.

02-edward-st-germain-and-his-sister-deli.title: Edward St. Germain and his sister Delia, mill workers, Phoenix, Rhode Island, April 1909
02-edward-st-germain-and-his-sister-deli.alt: The image shows a group of young individuals standing in front of a wooden building with horizontal siding.
02-edward-st-germain-and-his-sister-deli.description: Lewis Hine. Edward St. Germain and his sister Delia, mill workers, Phoenix, Rhode Island, April 1909, April 1909. National Gallery of Art.

03-wagon-boy-or-tail-boy-helping-to-load.title: Wagon boy or "tail boy" helping to load the wagon
03-wagon-boy-or-tail-boy-helping-to-load.alt: This is a photograph of a street scene in front of a shop.
03-wagon-boy-or-tail-boy-helping-to-load.description: Lewis Hine. Wagon boy or "tail boy" helping to load the wagon, c. 1914. National Gallery of Art.
